{{Short description|Statistics concept}}
{{Distinguish|Inter-rater reliability}}
In [[statistics]], '''intra-rater reliability''' is the degree of agreement among repeated administrations of a diagnostic test performed by a single rater.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.medicine.mcgill.ca/strokengine-assess/definitions-en.html |title=Stroke Engine glossary (McGill Faculty of Medicine) |access-date=2010-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100309071247/http://www.medicine.mcgill.ca/strokengine-assess/definitions-en.html |archive-date=2010-03-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.outcomesdatabase.org/show/category/id/8 |title=Outcomes database glossary |access-date=2010-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100423164517/http://www.outcomesdatabase.org/show/category/id/8 |archive-date=2010-04-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Intra-rater reliability and [[inter-rater reliability]] are aspects of [[test validity]].
